chain.label: Flight crew fatigued after 16+ hours awake, landing near normal bedtime
chain.trigger: the captain's prolonged wakefulness and the time of the accident... made it 'highly likely' that the captain was fatigued at the time of the crash

chain.label: Night operation with severe thunderstorm approaching airport
chain.trigger: The accident occurred during the hours of darkness.

chain.label: Line of severe thunderstorms moves over Little Rock airport during approach
chain.trigger: a northeast-to-southwest-oriented band of weather, with several large areas indicating reflectivities of level 6 (extreme) activity, encompassing the Little Rock airport area

chain.label: Heavy rain and RVR collapse from 3,000 to 1,600 feet on final
chain.trigger: the controller reported that there was heavy rain at the airport... the runway visual range (RVR) for runway 4R was 3,000 feet... At 2348:12, the controller reported that the runway 4R RVR was now 1,600 feet.

caused_by.evidence: heavy rain at the airport... visibility was less than 1 mile

chain.label: Crosswind of 20-34 knots exceeded company wet-runway/low-RVR limit
chain.trigger: The latest winds reported by the controller resulted in a crosswind component of 23 knots for the steady-state wind and 34 knots for the gusting wind... the maximum landing crosswind component is 15 knots

caused_by.evidence: the controller notified flight 1420 of a windshear alert... the wind was 350º at 30 knots gusting to 45 knots

chain.label: Crew never verified crosswind limit in flight manual; first officer misread wind back as 030 at 45
chain.trigger: the first officer stated that neither he nor the captain checked the actual crosswind limitation in American's flight manual... The first officer then read back the wind information as 030º at 45 knots.

caused_by.evidence: it can be more difficult for a fatigued person to remember whether tasks have been accomplished

chain.label: Crew's intent to beat the storm; approach not discontinued despite deteriorating cues
chain.trigger: the flight crew's failure to discontinue the approach when severe thunderstorms and their associated hazards to flight operations had moved into the airport area

caused_by.evidence: impaired performance resulting from fatigue and the situational stress associated with the intent to land under the circumstances
the dispatcher suggested that the flight crew expedite the arrival to beat the thunderstorms

there were cues... that the weather at and around the airport had deteriorated substantially. However, the CVR contained no discussion between the flight crewmembers about whether the approach should continue
continuation of the approach to a landing when the company's maximum crosswind component was exceeded
the flight crew likely did not recognize that an operational criterion for conducting the landing had been exceeded because the incorrect wind information read back by the first officer

chain.label: Before Landing checklist rushed and incomplete; spoiler handle never armed
chain.trigger: there is no CVR evidence to indicate that the first officer called out that the spoiler lever was armed... the spoilers did not automatically deploy because the spoiler handle was not armed by either pilot before landing

caused_by.evidence: the first officer did not ensure that the autospoilers had been armed for landing, and the captain did not realize that he had not called for flaps 40
the flight crew's earlier decision to accept a short approach increased the crew's already high workload by compressing the amount of time that was available to accomplish required tasks

chain.label: Unstabilized approach: localizer/glideslope deviations, sink rate warnings, 25 knots above Vref
chain.trigger: the CVR recorded the sound of the ground proximity warning system (GPWS) radio altitude callout 'sink rate'... airspeed averaged 156 knots, which was about 25 knots faster than the Vref

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew's failure to adequately prepare for the approach and the rapidly deteriorating weather conditions
FDR data showing fluctuating airspeed... were consistent with the presence of gusty and turbulent winds

chain.label: Touchdown 2,000 ft down runway at 160 knots ground speed with 5-knot tailwind
chain.trigger: The airplane touched down 2,000 feet from the runway threshold at a ground speed of 160 knots, drifting about 5º to the right, and a tailwind component of about 5 knots was present

caused_by.evidence: A ground speed of 160 knots was about 20 knots faster than the zero-wind touchdown ground speed

chain.label: Spoilers do not deploy at touchdown; crew fails to detect or manually extend them
chain.trigger: the crew's failure to ensure that the spoilers had extended after touchdown

caused_by.evidence: the autospoiler system operated properly and the spoilers did not automatically deploy because the spoiler handle was not armed
the flight crew failed to verify that the spoilers had automatically deployed after landing and... the captain failed to manually extend the spoilers when they did not deploy

chain.label: Reverse thrust applied well above the 1.3 EPR wet-runway limit (up to 1.98 EPR)
chain.trigger: use of reverse thrust greater than 1.3 engine pressure ratio after landing... The left engine reached a maximum setting of 1.98 reverse EPR

caused_by.evidence: the captain was likely applying excessive reverse thrust because he perceived that the landing had become an emergency situation

chain.label: Directional control lost on runway; airplane drifts up to 16 degrees and departs left side
chain.trigger: Flight 1420 continued to drift while on the runway by as much as 16º both to the right and the left of the direction of travel

caused_by.evidence: the light loading of the landing gear substantially reduced... the ability of the gear to develop cornering loads to counter the aerodynamic side loads produced by the crosswind
the use of reverse thrust at levels greater than 1.3 EPR significantly reduced the effectiveness of the airplane's rudder and vertical stabilizer and resulted in further directional control problems
The wind was blowing mostly along the airplane's lateral axis, from the left to the right sides of the airplane

chain.label: Airplane overruns departure end of runway 4R at 97 knots
chain.trigger: Flight 1420 departed the end of runway 4R sliding to the left... at a calculated speed of 97 knots.

caused_by.evidence: the lack of spoiler deployment was the single most important factor in the flight crew's inability to stop the accident airplane within the available runway length
its nose gear on the left edge of the runway and the main gear off the left edge of the runway

chain.label: Collision with nonfrangible runway 22L approach lighting structure at 83 knots; fuselage breaks up and burns
chain.trigger: collided with the structure supporting the runway 22L approach lighting system... The airplane was destroyed by impact forces and a postcrash fire.

caused_by.evidence: impacted the runway 22L approach lighting system support structure at about 83 knots

chain.label: Captain and 10 passengers killed; 45 serious and 65 minor injuries
chain.trigger: The captain and 10 passengers were killed; the first officer, the flight attendants, and 105 passengers received serious or minor injuries

caused_by.evidence: the airplane's collision with the nonfrangible approach lighting system was the direct cause of the fatal blunt force trauma injuries
